title: Incremental Reconciliation Gatekeeper for Replay & Backfill
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem statement:
We frequently run targeted backfills and replay jobs against the console usage pipelines to repair missing metrics and correct schema drift. Large-scale reprocess runs risk introducing duplicates, regressing derived metrics, or overwhelming downstream aggregation jobs. Current tooling either (a) replays whole time windows without fine-grained idempotency, or (b) requires heavy operator coordination to split and validate segments. We need a lightweight, incremental gatekeeper that orchestrates segmented replays with sanity checks, resumability, and automated quarantine for suspect segments.

Goals:
- Provide a coordinator service that accepts an ordered list of segment tokens and applies them incrementally with pre- and post-validation hooks.
- Ensure idempotent application of replays: dedupe by event fingerprint and replay-run id, maintain resume tokens on success/failure.
- Implement a quarantine step: if segment-level validation fails, isolate the segment for manual review without halting the whole backfill.
- Expose observability (per-segment status, validation diffs, token checkpoints) to Console dashboards and the backfill runbook.
- Support dry-run/preview mode that produces a validation diff without mutating downstream state.

Design notes / trade-offs:
- We will rely on existing prefix KV caching and the streaming reingest pathway instead of creating a parallel ingestion path to minimize surface area. Trade-off: small infra coupling with runtime caches but faster iteration and fewer integration points.
- Validation will be two-tier: lightweight schema & checksum checks executed inline, plus an optional heavier statistics diff job that runs asynchronously and updates the segment status. This balances speed with safety.
- To avoid long-running locks, the coordinator will use lease-based ownership per-segment (TTL + renew). This requires careful tuning of TTLs across AWS Lambda/worker timeouts.
- We considered per-tenant snapshotting; deferred due to cost. Plan a future enhancement to snapshot state for high-risk customers.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Coordinator service (new microservice) that: accepts a backfill manifest, slices into segments, publishes segment tasks to the reprocess queue, tracks segment checkpoints, and exposes a REST control API.
2) Segment worker: consumes tasks, runs replay through existing reingest pipeline with a replay-run id header, performs inline validations, emits results to a verdict topic.
3) Quarantine store: small DynamoDB table (or existing metastore) to hold failed segment payloads + diagnostics; flagged segments are removed from active queue and surfaced to the Console.
4) Observability: create a per-run dashboard (Grafana/Console) showing throughput, validation pass rate, expected vs applied deltas, and a diff artifact per-segment stored in S3 for manual inspection.
5) Safety switches: max-concurrent-segments per-run, rate-limiter per-tenant, automated pause-on-threshold for validation-failure-rate.

Artifacts and links:
- PRD: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Incremental+Reconciliation+Gatekeeper (draft)
- Design sketch: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1xGatekeeperDesignSketch
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1287
- Runbook draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Backfill+Gatekeeper+Runbook

Testing & rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (canary): run on synthetic tenant with small history (3 days) in staging. Run dry-run mode and validate diffs match expectations.
- Phase 2 (shadow): run coordinator in production but with dry-run on a low-volume customer; surface diffs to console without applying.
- Phase 3 (small apply): apply to a single internal tenant with supervised monitoring and automatic rollback on >5% validation failure in first 100 segments.
- Phase 4 (gradual): increase concurrency and tenant coverage with automated quarantine enabled.

Monitoring & metrics to track:
- segments_submitted, segments_processed, segments_quarantined, per_segment_validation_time, applied_events_count, deduped_events_count, replay_error_rate.
- Dashboard: console-analytics/backfill/gatekeeper-run/{run_id}

Rollback & recovery:
- Each segment stores a resume token and applied_event_fingerprint summary. If a regression is detected, we can replay only post-failure segments or restore a downstream snapshot when available. Quarantined segments are manually inspected and can be requeued after patching.

Open questions / future work:
- Whether to store full event slices vs pointers to S3 for quarantine (cost vs debug ability).
- Integration with Dedicated customers who may require on-prem replay tooling (API contract differences).
- Automated remediation: can we implement a small class of automatic fixes (schema normalization) before quarantining?
acceptance_criteria: Coordinator accepts manifest and produces a run_id with segment tokens
Segment worker applies replay with replay-run id and reports verdict status
Quarantine store holds failure diagnostics and prevents failed segments from being applied
Dry-run mode produces diffs without mutating downstream state
Dashboard surfaces per-segment status and basic validation metrics
Automated pause triggers when validation-failure-rate exceeds configured threshold
comments: 2025-02-12 - Ava Martinez: Created ticket and draft PRD. Assigned to Ravi for initial design and spike.

2025-02-18 - Ravi Patel: Completed spike. Prototype shown in standup; discovered that reingest path strips replay-run headers for batched writes — created a follow-up PR to propagate headers (PR #1287).
2025-02-22 - Priya Nair (Data Eng): Reviewed design. Concern about DynamoDB hot keys for quarantine table; recommended shard key by run_id+segment_idx. Added as implementation note.

2025-02-25 - Security (Oliver Chen): Quick review: no PII retention in quarantine blobs by default; require operator opt-in. Marked security_review_required = false for now but flagged for future review if we change retention policy.

2025-03-02 - Ravi Patel: Implemented basic coordinator and published staging deployment. Began canary dry-runs against synthetic tenant. Observed 0.8% mismatch in checksum validation due to timezone offset; added normalization step.

2025-03-05 - QA (Lina Gomez): Performed integration test run. Found race where worker renew lease after upstream pipeline completes causing duplicate apply attempts. Proposed lease TTL reduction and stronger idempotency checks. Added follow-up sub-issue ENG-422110.
